title: Purpose → Plan → Result
summary: A remembered Witcher phrase becomes a prompt to separate a problem's purpose, proposed approach, and observable outcome.
epitaph: The plan was never a prophecy.
revive_when: A Problem Space sketch needs a clear purpose, a testable approach, and a way to recognize whether anything improved.

related.reason: Separating purpose from plan makes it easier to keep a useful aim while discarding an approach that no longer serves it.
Purpose, plan, and result map onto the eulogy's original problem, attempted approach, and account of what actually exists.

sources.label: Blathan Caerme — secondary essay reproducing the wording and attributing it to The Tower of the Swallow
Orbit / Hachette — The Tower of Swallows, Andrzej Sapkowski, translated by David French (bibliographic source)

origin: User supplied a conversational note recalling a phrase attributed to Andrzej Sapkowski's The Tower of the Swallow and suggesting a Problem Space connection; the note's original author is unknown. The caretaker found matching wording in a secondary essay and added the practical prompts and collection connections. Attribution was not checked against a primary edition; the literary quotation retains its original rights.
